subject: Miscalculation of Variance when Fitting SEM

messages.author: 50582e01ff92742f
messages.subject: Miscalculation of Variance when Fitting SEM
parts:
Hey, all!

I conducted a principal component analysis with oblimin rotation in SPSS with a dataset of 199 subjects and 37 items (I know this is not optimal). I obtained a decent 6-factor solution that makes theoretical sense, and I wanted to visualize the model. The problem is that when I attempt to fit the model to my dataset (the same dataset the model is derived from) in R, the variance of one item is grossly miscalculated. lavaan reports the variance as -16646.373, which besides being impossible, is also insanely far off of the actual variance of this item of 70.10949. The responses for this item are not very different from the responses to any other items, so I'm not sure why the calculation is failing on this item and none of the other items. If I remove this item from the model, lavaan can fit the data as expected. Any suggestions on how to address this error? Why might this be occurring? Further, how can I visualize my model with lavaanPlot when fitting the model fails?

Thanks, Jonah
